title: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement Antwerp | Ships & Tankers
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Antwerp: chemical tanker cargo piping UTM, hull structure gauging, CAP and ESP renewal survey support at berth or dock.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Tankers and Ships in Antwerp
intro: Antwerp combines Europe's second-largest port with its largest integrated chemical cluster, and the ships that serve it are the ones that most need careful gauging: coated and stainless chemical parcel tankers, gas carriers, product tankers and a deep-sea container and ro-ro fleet. Superintendents bring us in for UTM in Antwerp on cargo and ballast piping, ESP structure and pre-docking estimates while the ship is inside the dock system. A team flies in from India for each vessel and joins the ship in Antwerp.

highlights.p: Parcel tankers moving between chemical jetties carry aggressive cargoes through long runs of cargo piping. Wall-thickness checks on lines and deck manifolds fit tank-cleaning stops, and ballast tank structure, often the first to waste, is gauged in the same visit.

Most chemical and breakbulk terminals lie behind the Berendrecht, Zandvliet, Kallo or Kieldrecht locks. Ships inside the dock system often shift berths and wait between parcels, which gives realistic windows for ballast tank and hold gauging.

The floating docks at EDR Antwerp Shipyard take tankers, bulk carriers and cargo ships into dock inside the port. Pre-docking readings taken at the cargo berth let the yard plan steel before the vessel even shifts.

port.h: Antwerp's docks, its chemical cluster and the ships that serve it
p: The Port of Antwerp-Bruges, formed when Antwerp and Zeebrugge merged, is Europe's second-largest port, and its Antwerp half lies far up the tidal Scheldt. Deep-sea container ships work the tidal terminals on the river and at the Deurganck dock, while behind the big sea locks a network of docks serves breakbulk, steel, cars, high-and-heavy cargo and, above all, the petrochemical industry. The refineries, steam crackers and chemical plants along the right and left banks make Antwerp a hub for chemical parcel tankers, product tankers and liquefied gas carriers, alongside a large fleet of inland tank barges.

The geography gives ships reasons to stay. Passage of the Westerschelde is piloted and, for deep-draught ships, timed to the tide, so arrival and departure are fixed points around which everything else is planned. Inside the lock-bound docks, a chemical tanker discharging several parcels may shift between a number of jetties over several days, with waiting time between them for berths, cargo surveyors and tank cleaning. Breakbulk and ro-ro ships load in stages, and ships that miss a berth either anchor at sea off the Scheldt mouth or lie at lay-by quays inside the docks until one comes free. EDR Antwerp Shipyard docks vessels inside the port, and other repair contractors carry out afloat work at repair quays.

Inspection demand in Antwerp is concentrated on cargo systems. Chemical cargoes, and the cleaning cycles between them, attack cargo piping, deck lines and the coatings of ballast tanks next to heated cargo tanks. Chemical tankers fall under the ESP Code and IACS UR Z10.3, so from the third renewal survey, at around fifteen years, gauging of cargo and ballast tank structure becomes extensive, and parcel-tanker charterers ask detailed questions about structural condition during vetting. Product tankers serving the refineries add oil-major vetting and, on older ships, requests for a CAP grading. Gas carriers bring their own priorities around deck piping, hold spaces and the structure surrounding tank domes.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens inside the port of Antwerp
p: Antwerp ship repair for deep-sea tonnage centres on EDR Antwerp Shipyard, whose floating docks inside the port take tankers, bulk carriers, cargo ships and offshore units. Because the yard sits within the same dock system as the cargo terminals, a superintendent can have the ship gauged at its last discharge berth, send the readings to the yard, and arrive with the steel programme already defined. Repair contractors working alongside at repair quays handle afloat jobs, and gauging can define the scope of those repairs too.

Afloat, the chemical jetties are the most common workplace and the most regulated. Each terminal applies its own permit-to-work and gas-detection rules, and cargo tank entry needs cleaning, ventilation and a gas-free certificate. Deck manifolds, cargo and ballast lines and pump-room piping can usually be measured during or between operations with the right permits. Container terminals on the river allow little more than deck, lashing-bridge and scrubber piping checks within a working call, while breakbulk and ro-ro berths inside the docks offer more time. For ships awaiting a berth, the lay-by quays in the dock system are often the best compromise between access and time.
list: EDR Antwerp Shipyard — pre-docking and in-dock gauging on tankers, bulk carriers and cargo ships using its floating docks inside the port.
Chemical jetties on the right and left banks — cargo piping, manifold and pump-room wall-thickness checks on parcel tankers under terminal permits.
Liquefied gas berths — deck piping, hold-space and tank-surround gauging on LPG and ethylene carriers between cargo operations.
Deurganck dock and river container terminals — exhaust-gas scrubber discharge lines, lashing bridges and hatch coamings measured while the ship works its call.
Breakbulk, steel and ro-ro berths inside the locks — hold, tank-top, ramp and car-deck gauging on multipurpose and ro-ro ships during staged loading.
Lay-by quays in the dock system — ballast tank and cargo-tank gauging on ships waiting between parcels or for a yard slot, once gas-free.

context.h: Port state control, emissions rules and the Antwerp tanker market
p: Belgium applies Paris MoU port state control, and Antwerp, its approaches and the whole Scheldt passage are inside the North Sea SOx ECA, where marine fuel may carry no more than 0.10% sulphur. Scrubber-fitted ships therefore either burn compliant fuel on the river or operate their exhaust gas cleaning systems under whatever local wash-water rules apply in Belgian and Dutch waters, which the agent should confirm for each call. Antwerp is also a major bunkering port, so many ships change fuel here, and those stops are useful moments to inspect wash-water and overboard lines.

The local owner and operator community gives the market a technical edge. Antwerp has long been home to tanker and gas carrier owners and managers, and chemical tanker charterers apply detailed vetting that looks hard at structural condition and cargo system integrity. With shipping brought into EU ETS in 2024 and FuelEU Maritime applying from 2025, the owner of an older parcel tanker or product tanker weighs those obligations against the steel renewal due at its next ESP survey before deciding whether to keep it trading. Measured thickness data, gathered on a call before the decision, makes that comparison concrete.

jobs.h: Typical gauging requests for ships in Antwerp
jobs.p: Antwerp jobs are shaped by the cargo plan. A tanker's sequence of jetties, cleaning stops and berth waits decides when spaces can be opened, and the superintendent usually wants the gauging threaded through that sequence rather than holding the ship. Dockings at EDR Antwerp Shipyard follow the TM plan and the survey programme instead. Typical requests from Antwerp include the following.
list: A coated chemical parcel tanker approaching its third ESP renewal: cargo and ballast tank structure gauged during a cleaning stop between Antwerp parcels, then completed in dock.
A stainless-steel chemical tanker with suspect deck lines: wall-thickness survey of cargo piping, manifolds and steam lines on deck while waiting for a jetty.
An LPG carrier discharging at a gas berth: deck piping, hold-space structure and ballast tank gauging under the terminal's permit system.
A product tanker asked for a CAP grading by a charterer: CAP thickness measurement of cargo and ballast tanks after cleaning, on a lay-by quay inside the locks.
A ro-ro ship loading high-and-heavy cargo: ramp, car-deck and stern structure gauging during a staged loading call, ahead of the intermediate survey.

logistics: Brussels Airport is the main international gateway, with road and rail connections to Antwerp; the city's own small airport handles only limited regional flights. Terminals and the yard sit inside ISPS-controlled port areas on both banks, and the ship's agent registers the team for gate access and, where needed, for a terminal safety induction. A technician travelling from India needs a Schengen visa before entering Belgium, so give us the expected arrival window and berth plan as early as possible and we will schedule mobilisation around the cargo sequence.

faqs.q: Can you gauge cargo piping on a chemical tanker while it moves between Antwerp jetties?
faqs.a: Yes, if the terminal permits it and the lines are drained and isolated. Deck lines, manifolds and pump-room piping are typically measured during the waiting time between parcels. We work within the ship's permit-to-work arrangements and the jetty's own requirements, and report wall loss against nominal and minimum thickness so the superintendent can decide on renewals before the next cargo.

faqs.q: Do lock passages limit when the team can board?
faqs.a: They set the timetable. Ships entering the dock system through the Berendrecht, Zandvliet, Kallo or Kieldrecht locks arrive on a scheduled slot, and deep-draught ships on the river follow the tide. The team's travel is timed to the agent's berth estimate; we board once the ship is safely alongside, and adjust if the lock or tidal plan changes.

faqs.q: Is stainless-steel cargo tank structure gauged differently?
faqs.a: The ultrasonic method is the same, but the gauge is calibrated for the sound velocity of the material and probe choice is adjusted, and readings on stainless tank structure are reported separately from the carbon-steel ballast and hull structure. Wastage patterns differ too: stainless tanks are rarely the limiting factor, while the carbon-steel ballast tanks and cofferdams around them often are.

faqs.q: Can gauging in Antwerp feed a docking at EDR Antwerp Shipyard?
faqs.a: That is a common sequence. The ship is gauged at its last cargo berth, readings are mapped to the TM plan with renewal candidates marked, and the superintendent shares them with the yard. The yard plans steel and docking days on measured data, and in dock the team completes the remaining spaces and supports the class surveyor's close-up survey.
